summary: The base defect was reproduced and the candidate fixes delayed-versus-cached OFFLINE TTFT when time.time() and time.perf_counter() advance equally, while preserving BLOCKING behavior. It is not a complete fix because it adds a perf_counter duration to a time.time timestamp. When the wall clock and monotonic clock diverge, last_real_time_ts moves into the future and legitimate non-predictor CPU overhead is suppressed. The candidate should measure and update the exclusion in one clock domain.

tests.what_was_measured: Actual scheduler hooks on the prepared base. The normal-clock OFFLINE cold/cached test failed (0.440/0.141 seconds rather than 0.190/0.140), reproducing predictor wall-time contamination; the BLOCKING semantics case passed. Evidence: /job/review-evidence/base/reproduction-final.txt

All four candidate regression cases passed with optional AIConfigurator imports stubbed: OFFLINE and BLOCKING, with cold-first and cached-first predictor delays. Evidence: /job/review-evidence/candidate/candidate-regression-with-dependency-stubs.txt

Normal-clock OFFLINE invariance and BLOCKING preservation passed. The independent mismatched-clock case failed: expected 0.145/0.095 seconds but got 0.100/0.0945, proving legitimate CPU overhead can be removed by combining perf_counter duration with a time.time timestamp. Evidence: /job/review-evidence/candidate/independent-clock-tests.txt
The candidate source and regression-test changes have no whitespace errors. Candidate-added raw report artifacts were excluded because they contain pre-existing captured trailing whitespace.

gpu_execution_evidence: The prepared interpreter sees an AMD Instinct MI355X with Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2, but this host-clock scheduler review did not execute GPU kernels. The reported NVIDIA H200/CUDA 13.0 benchmark cannot be reproduced on this architecture.
remaining_counterexamples: If perf_counter advances 250 ms while time.time advances 125 ms during a predictor call, the candidate advances last_real_time_ts by 250 ms. The following OFFLINE accounting clamps CPU overhead to zero and reports 100 ms TTFT instead of the 145 ms modeled-plus-legitimate-host-overhead reference.
The timestamp remains ahead after the first iteration, so the clock-domain error can leak into later iterations and suppress additional legitimate overhead.
remaining_limitations: The exact H200, Qwen3.6-27B weights, and h200_sxm AIConfigurator database were unavailable; the original end-to-end numerical benchmark was not rerun.
The prepared host is AMD Instinct MI355X/ROCm 7.2 rather than NVIDIA H200/CUDA 13.0.

The prepared interpreter lacked simulator optional dependencies. The focused scheduler-hook tests used minimal import stubs and isolated joblib/scikit-learn packages; no real AIConfigurator database query was executed.
No native source changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
